review: The hymn is the blood's power as a call to the unconverted: 1:1–4 is 1 Pet 1:19 with Zech 13:1, 2:1–4 is Heb 2:14–15 with Col 2:15, 3:1–4 is 1 John 1:7 with Isa 1:18, 4:1–4 is Ps 51:9 (תְּלַבְּנֵנִי מִשֶּׁלֶג) with Heb 4:16, and 5:1–4 is Rom 6:18 with Phil 4:13.

The two refrains are printed with different verbs (هَا قَدْ ظَفَر 'triumphant' in the odd lines, قَدْ قَهَر 'He conquered' in the even), and the Hebrew keeps the distinction: הִנֵּה נִצַּח against כִּי כָבַשׁ.

1:2 דְּמֵי הַפָּצוּעַ — the Arabic دَمِ ذَاكَ الْجَرِيح is 'the blood of that wounded One'; the Hebrew uses the plural דָּמִים, the form Gen 4:10 and 2 Sam 3:28 use for blood shed in violence, so the line names a death and not a fluid.

3:3 הִטָּהֲרוּ — the Arabic تَطَهَّرْ is a singular imperative inside a plural address; the Hebrew pluralises it to match its own addressees, since the stanza speaks to the crowd and the print's shift is a copyist's smoothing.
